frameLabelResolver.role: Parses the SWF tag stream directly (stdlib zlib/struct only) to compute REAL 1-based animation frame numbers for each named FrameLabel tag inside a chosen DefineSprite, by counting ShowFrame tags. This is more reliable than ffdec's -dumpSWF text output, whose per-line counters are nested-tag-list positions, not frame numbers.

sheetPacker.role: Packs a contiguous run of ffdec-exported per-frame PNGs into one horizontal sprite-sheet PNG matching the coUserver Spritesheet grid model (frameWidth x frameHeight x numFrames, single row). Fails if frames are missing or of inconsistent size.

bitmapExtractor.role: Diagnostic/fallback: extracts embedded raster tags (DefineBits*/DefineBitsLossless*) directly without rendering, for source SWFs that DO bake bitmaps rather than vectors. Run against both selected sources first; both reported zero bitmap tags (161 and 24 unextracted vector shape tags respectively), which is why ffdec rendering was required instead of a simpler direct-extract path.

SCALE BUGFIX (2026-08-28): originally packed at the raw ffdec per-frame canvas size 414x291 -- 5-6x the angle states' scale, confirmed via a live screenshot to render comically oversized (bigger than a tree). Root cause: ffdec's exported per-frame canvas for this DefineSprite is sized to the UNION of the shape's extent across the whole clip's own timeline, and this clip's timeline bakes in the creature translating/wobbling a large distance within its own local coordinate space (verified frame-by-frame: e.g. fly-side's bbox y-range moved from y=3-262 at frame 1 to y=200-428 at frame 20 of the same 479px-tall canvas) -- i.e. camera-relative flight-path motion baked into the nested MovieClip bounds, not a genuinely larger creature. The angle1/angle2/rest-angle* states' art doesn't move within its own frame, so their canvas stayed tight. Fix: uniformly downscaled the already-packed sheet (PIL LANCZOS resize of the whole horizontal strip in one pass, so frame boundaries stay exact multiples of the new frame width -- no per-frame rounding drift) so the largest frame dimension matches fly-angle1's 78px, preserving the aspect ratio and all baked-in motion (now proportionally smaller, as it should be for a same-size creature). Before: 414x291. After: 78x55 (scale factor 78/414=0.1884).
